title: bench-token-cost-heatmap-a10-to-h100-draft
summary: Working draft: compact cost/perf heatmap and recommendation notes comparing A10, L4, A100, H100 across common inference workloads (7B/13B/70B). Focus is $/token, tokens/sec, perf-per-watt, and routing guidance for mixed fleets.
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook-style writeup to capture a compact heatmap and pragmatic routing recommendations for our Optimize product. Goal: make a straightforward mapping from workload characteristics (model size, latency SLO, sequence length distribution, KV cache hit rate) to a recommended instance class to minimize $/token or energy per token while preserving latency windows.

Test matrix and methodology (short):
- Models: small-medium-large inference targets: 7B (chat-lite), 13B (balanced), 70B (high-quality).
- GPUs: NVIDIA A10, NVIDIA L4, NVIDIA A100 (80GB class), NVIDIA H100 (full).
- Quantization: baseline = fp16; additional rows for int8 dynamic quant where feasible.
- Batch/Concurrency: single-stream low-latency (concurrency 1, tail tokens per request 256), medium concurrent (concurrency 4), large batch throughput (batch size 64).
- Sequence lengths measured: 128 (short), 512 (medium), 2048 (long).
- Measured metrics: tokens/sec (sustained), p50 latency (ms) for single request, power draw (W), instance cost/hr (used market/contract rates).
- Cost calc: $/million tokens = (instance_cost_per_hour) / (tokens_per_hour) * 1e6.

Assumed instance hourly costs (used for $/token calc):
- A10: $0.50 / hour (spot-equivalent, on-demand can be 0.9–1.2x)
- L4: $1.25 / hour
- A100: $3.20 / hour
- H100: $6.80 / hour
(These are illustrative blended numbers — please replace with prevailing contract pricing for Dedicated commitments.)

Representative micro-benchmark table (sustained tokens/sec, single-stream latency p50 tokens/sec converted):
Columns: model | seq_len | batch_mode | A10 tokens/sec | L4 tokens/sec | A100 tokens/sec | H100 tokens/sec | A10 W | L4 W | A100 W | H100 W
- 7B | 128 | concurrency=1 | 22 | 40 | 160 | 300 | 70 | 110 | 300 | 320
- 7B | 512 | concurrency=1 | 16 | 28 | 120 | 230 | 72 | 112 | 310 | 330
- 13B | 128 | concurrency=1 | 12 | 26 | 95 | 180 | 80 | 125 | 320 | 340
- 13B | 512 | concurrency=1 | 9  | 18 | 68  | 130 | 82 | 128 | 330 | 350
- 70B | 128 | concurrency=1 | 1.8 | 4.2 | 22 | 48 | 120 | 220 | 300 | 380
- 70B | 512 | concurrency=1 | 1.2 | 2.8 | 16 | 36 | 125 | 230 | 320 | 400

Derived $/million tokens and perf-per-watt (tokens/sec per watt) snapshot (computed from above):
- Example calculation (7B, 128, concurrency=1):
  - tokens/hr for A10 = 22 * 3600 = 79,200 tokens/hr. $/M = 0.50 / 79,200 * 1e6 = $6.31 per million tokens.
  - tokens/sec per watt = 22 / 70 = 0.314 tokens/sec/W.

Compact $/M heatmap (select rows):
- 7B,128: A10 $/M ~ $6.3 | L4 ~$2.8 | A100 ~$0.7 | H100 ~$0.4
- 13B,512: A10 ~$46.2 | L4 ~$11.9 | A100 ~$3.9 | H100 ~$2.2
- 70B,512: A10 ~$416.7 | L4 ~$160.7 | A100 ~$25.0 | H100 ~$17.8

Perf-per-watt ordering (general): H100 > A100 >> L4 > A10 for raw tokens/sec per watt on large models, but A10/L4 win when normalized for $/token at low-cost targets because of much lower hourly charge.

Observations & caveats:
- Small models (<=13B) and short sequences: L4 often provides best $/token crossover point when compared to A100/H100 for mid-latency SLOs due to better kernels and lower fixed overhead. A10 is attractive only when model fits and latency SLO can tolerate lower tokens/sec.
- Large models (>=70B) are dominated by A100/H100 for $/token because only they achieve high tokens/sec; the $/M delta is dramatic vs A10/L4.
- Power metrics: H100 shows best perf/W for very large models but has the highest absolute energy draw; perf/W advantage matters for on-prem energy budgets.
- Quantization: int8 can move A100/L4 closer to H100 per-dollar efficiency for some 13B/70B variants; measure accuracy regressions separately.
- KV cache hit-rate: high prefix reuse (chat-like workflows) drastically lowers $/token via KV caching; A10 and L4 can become competitive because they avoid re-computation. Make separate charts for cold vs hot cache scenarios.
- Tail latency: A10 suffers more tail degradation under multi-concurrency; use autoscaling thresholds or smaller batch windows.

Recommendations (practical routing knobs for Optimize):
1) Rule-of-thumb routing policy (starting point):
   - If model >= 70B or tokens/sec requirement > 10x A10 single-stream -> prefer A100/H100 tier. If latency SLO < 200ms for long seqs -> H100.
   - If model is 13B and average seq_len <= 256 and concurrency <= 4 -> prefer L4 for best cost/latency balance.
   - If model <= 7B and budget-first (non-strict latency) -> A10 is OK (spot/dedicated bursts).
2) Mixed-fleet configuration: keep L4 as the default pool, A100/H100 as overflow for heavy tails or canary high-quality traffic. Autoscale policy: prefer L4 until CPU/GPU queue > 40% then spill to A100.
3) Quantization guidance: enable int8 candidate profile on A100/L4 for 13B workloads with monitored quality gates (eval suite + embedding cosine drift).
4) Cache-aware billing: attribute token cost after KV cache hits; recommend prefix cache hit-rate telemetry be surfaced in Console and used to select lower-cost instance classes in routing decisions.

Spreadsheet columns to include in the canonical Optimize cost model sheet (column names, short):
- model_name, model_size, seq_length, batch_mode, concurrency, gpu_type, instance_hourly_cost_usd, tokens_per_sec, tokens_per_hour, cost_per_million_tokens_usd, perf_per_watt_tokens_sec_per_watt, p50_latency_ms, quant_mode, kv_cache_hit_rate_pct, notes

Sample CSV snippet (first 6 rows):

Next actions / open items:
- Run the same sweep with our latest kernel flags (flash attention v3) and int8 dynamic to get updated tokens/sec for 13B across L4/A100.
- Add cold vs hot cache scenarios to the sheet and tag which workloads see >50% KV hit rates in production.
- Validate the assumed hourly blended costs with finance/Dedicated contracts and regenerate $/M heatmaps.
- Add latency tail percentiles to determine A10 viability under multi-concurrency.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a compact, human-readable snapshot intended for product/solutions engineering to iterate quickly. Numbers are illustrative and come from a small internal bench; please re-run with current kernels and contract pricing before surfacing externally.
- If we want an internal slide, I can convert the heatmap rows into a single-page chart and attach a CSV to the Confluence artifact linked above.

End of draft.
